title: Offline quota enforcement and delta-export format for air-gapped on-prem collectors
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement an idempotent, bandwidth-efficient delta export format for air-gapped on-prem usage collectors and extend on-node quota enforcement so that rate-limits applied locally converge correctly with the central ledger after delayed sync. This ticket covers format design, ingestion semantics, crypto signing, reconciliation logic, and a safe rollout plan for existing private deployments.
background: Customers running Redwood Private currently rely on on-node collectors that buffer usage in a bundle file for periodic uplink. We have several pain points: large bundle sizes for high-throughput tenants, duplicated or out-of-order records causing over/under billing, and local quota enforcement that doesn't account for delayed central reconciliation, which can lead to incorrect throttling or silent overage allowances. Existing implementations use coarse checkpointing which forces full-file uploads and leads to long reconcile windows.
goals: Define a compact, delta-first export format that supports incremental uploads (sequence vectors + chunked checksums)
Ensure on-node quota enforcement uses a convergent accounting model that tolerates offline increments and mitigates transient double-counting
Make ingestion idempotent and conflict-resilient on the central billing ledger
Keep CPU and storage overhead on constrained on-prem appliances minimal
Provide a migration and rollout plan that keeps customer request latency and rate-limit behavior stable
non_goals: Replace the entire ledger architecture in this ticket
Implement new UI features — console work tracked separately
Edge-case audits for unsupported old bundle formats (those are deprecated)
acceptance_criteria: Define and document the delta-export schema (fields, envelope, seq vectors, chunk checksums) and publish spec to Drive
On-node collector produces delta files under 1/4 the size of current full-bundles for typical workloads in our benchmark (see perf doc)
Ingestion service accepts delta bundles and is idempotent: repeated apply of same bundle doesn't change ledger after first apply
Central reconciliation resolves local vs central counters with a deterministic merge that never reduces previously reported usage (monotonicity) and produces auditable transforms
Local quota algorithm uses a conservative reserve strategy to avoid customer-visible over-throttles during sync and has a documented knob for aggressive vs conservative modes
Unit + integration tests for export/ingest/reconcile paths with simulated delayed uploads (0-72 hours) and conflict scenarios
Runbook updated with manual reconciliation and emergency rollback steps
Security review completed for bundle signing and KMS/HSM integration
implementation_steps: Design delta-export schema and write reference serializer in Go
Implement cryptographic envelope: bundle header with signer id, nonce, timestamp, and signature (support RSA-PSS and ed25519)
Add on-node sequencer producing monotonic usage IDs and chunk-level checksums (xxhash64)
Implement local quota enforcement extension: local token-bucket with conservative escrow and background drain based on confirmed central receipts
Backend ingestion endpoint: idempotent apply using (tenant, bundle_id, sequence_vector) and single-writer per-tenant ordering guard
Reconciliation worker: deterministic merge that sums confirmed deltas and marks residuals for manual review if checksums mismatch
Add telemetry: bundle arrival time, apply latency, conflict rate, bytes saved vs baseline
End-to-end tests + chaos tests: reorder bundles, duplicate uploads, partial uploads, and clock skew
migration_and_rollout: Phase 0 (canary): deploy serializer to 3 internal on-prem clusters; collectors emit both legacy full-bundle and delta-bundle in parallel
Phase 1: enable delta-only uploads for low-throughput customers with auditing enabled; ingestion accepts both formats
Phase 2: enable delta-only for all customers and flip default quota mode to conservative-escrow for 48 hours before switching aggressive mode configurable flag
Phase 3: remove legacy full-bundle write after 30 days of stable canaries and no reconciliation anomalies
Provide a migration script for customers who opted out of parallel mode to precompute sequence offsets
testing_plan: Unit tests for serializer/deserializer and signature verification
Integration harness that spins a local ledger and simulated on-node collector producing randomized deltas
Load test with 1k tenants emulating bursty request patterns to validate bundle sizing and CPU impact
Regression test verifying rate-limit behavior across sync delays of up to 72 hours
Fuzz tests for malformed bundles and missing chunks
observability_and_slo_checks: New metrics: delta_bundle_bytes, delta_apply_success, delta_apply_conflict, quota_local_denials, quota_reconciled_drains
Dashboards: ingestion latency heatmap, conflict rate over time, bytes saved per tenant tier
Alerting: delta_apply_conflict > 0.5% for 15m triggers P1 and paging
SLO: 99.9% delta bundle apply success within 30s for non-big bundles
security_considerations: Bundles MUST be signed with a rotation-capable key; support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) required
Replay protection via bundle_id + sequence_vector and server-side TTL for stale bundles
Audit logs for apply operations including signer id and resulting ledger deltas
Bundle encryption optional for high-compliance customers (support AES-GCM payloads)
Threat modeling session scheduled with Security team (link in links)
